the mishna: the thigh bone of sacrifices -- one who touches it, sealed or perforated, is impure
the mishna: the thigh bone of a carcass or of a creeping thing -- one who touches them sealed is pure
the mishna: perforated at all -- it imparts impurity by contact
one who touches [the corpse's thigh bone] -- yes [impure]; one who overlies it -- no
[the mishna speaks] where there is no olive-bulk of flesh
[the mishna speaks] where there is no olive-bulk of marrow inside
that is to say: marrow inside does not heal [the bone] outside
actually, marrow inside heals [the bone] outside
the first clause where there is no olive-bulk [of marrow], the latter clause where there is an olive-bulk
[the sacrifices clause teaches:] serving as a base to notar is significant
R' Yitzchak: bones of sacrifices that served notar impart impurity to the hands, since it became a base to a forbidden thing
R' Yitzchak's reason: since it became a base to a forbidden thing
[the carcass clause teaches:] even where there is an olive-bulk [of marrow], perforated -- yes; not perforated -- no
Abaye: here we deal with where he scraped it
R' Elazar: a thigh bone scraped lengthwise -- impure
R' Elazar: [scraped] widthwise -- pure; and your mnemonic: the palm
R' Yochanan: actually where there is an olive-bulk [of marrow]
R' Yochanan: and what is the 'touches' that it teaches? -- overlies

the mishna: one who touches a half olive-bulk and overlies a half olive-bulk, or a half olive-bulk overlies him -- impure
R' Avin: [contact and overlying] are one concept -- that is why they join
the mishna: this is the rule -- whatever is of one concept joins and is impure; of two concepts -- pure
the mishna's latter clause: one who touches a half olive-bulk, and another thing overlies him and a half olive-bulk -- pure
R' Zeira: we deal with impurity pressed between two chests with no handbreadth opening between them, for all of it is touching
who is the tanna who calls a tent 'touching'? it is R' Yosei

a full ladle of grave-dust imparts impurity by carrying
a full ladle of grave-dust imparts impurity in a tent

Abaye: [overlying] below a handbreadth is a touching-tent
Abaye: [overlying] above a handbreadth is a mere tent
Rava: even above a handbreadth it is a touching-tent

R' Yosei: bed-bundles and window grilles interpose between the house and the upper floor, not to let impurity into the other side
R' Yosei: spread them over a corpse in the air -- one who touches opposite the hole is impure
R' Yosei: not opposite the hole -- pure

R' Yosei holds: hidden impurity does not break through
the first tanna: a chest compartment with a handbreadth inside and no handbreadth in its opening -- impurity inside it, the house is impure
the first tanna: impurity in the house -- what is inside it is pure
the first tanna: because impurity's way is to go out, and impurity's way is not to go in
R' Yosei declares [the house] pure
R' Yosei: because one can remove it in halves, or burn it in its place
the latter clause: set in the doorway opening outward -- impurity inside it, the house is pure; impurity in the house, what is inside it is pure
[the horn:] R' Yosei's 'declares pure' stands on the latter clause
[the horn:] R' Yosei's 'declares pure' stands on the first clause

R' Yosei: one looks -- from opposite the lintel inward, the house is impure
R' Yosei: from opposite the lintel outward, the house is pure
R' Elazar: its mouth inward -- the house is pure
R' Elazar: its mouth outward -- the house is impure, because the impurity exits by way of its rear
R' Yehuda ben Beteira: either way -- the house is impure
Rava: '[one looks at] the hollow of the impurity' is what it teaches
Rava: R' Yosei disputes [R' Meir] on two points
Rava [for R' Yosei, to R' Meir]: we go by its hollow
R' Yosei says: one looks at the hollow of the impurity

R' Shimon: three impurities separate from a corpse, two [modes] in each one and the third not in them
R' Shimon: a ladle of grave-dust does not impart impurity by contact; where is its contact? with one of them
R' Shimon: a barley-grain bone imparts impurity by carrying
R' Shimon: a barley-grain bone imparts impurity by contact
R' Shimon: [a barley-grain bone] does not impart impurity in a tent; where is its tent? with one of them

R' Shimon: a grave cover and wall impart impurity in a tent

objections.gloss_en: במאי אוקימתה? דליכא כזית. אי הכי, במוקדשים אמאי מטמא?

objections.gloss_en: ותהוי כטומאה טמונה בוקעת ועולה? -- below a handbreadth, let it be hidden impurity that breaks through

answered_by.gloss_en: קסבר רבי יוסי: טומאה טמונה אינה בוקעת (= p_ry_temuna_einah_bokaat)

objections.gloss_en: ורמי דרבי יוסי אדרבי יוסי, דתנן: the dog ... R' Yosei: from opposite the lintel inward the house is impure. מאי לאו אאין בצוארו פותח טפח קאי רבי יוסי? ושמע מינה טומאה טמונה בוקעת! (126a.8-9)
